guide.title: Trastevere (R. XIII), Rome: Fountains, the Janiculum and 1849
guide.intro: Trastevere is the thirteenth rione of Rome, R. XIII, on the right bank of the Tiber. it.wikipedia derives the name from the Latin trans Tiberim, beyond the Tiber, and states that the present rione corresponded to the fourteenth of the regions into which Augustus divided the territory of Rome, called Regio Transtiberim. it.wikipedia records that water arrived in 1612, when Paul V's Acqua Paola aqueduct reached the quarter; five of the fountains it fed have their own record in Roma Capitale's voice. Above the flat streets the Janiculum ridge carries the promenade, the ossuary and the monuments of the Roman Republic of 1849. This guide covers buildings, water and the Risorgimento. The trattorie, bakeries, cinemas and the Porta Portese flea market are not here, because no source for them could be fetched.

sections.heading: What the rione is, and where its edges run
sections.body: it.wikipedia records Trastevere as R. XIII and states its boundaries: the Mura gianicolensi to the south and west, the Principe Amedeo Savoia-Aosta tunnel to the north, and the Tiber to the east. Its neighbours are Borgo to the north; Ponte, Regola, Ripa and Testaccio to the east across the river; and Aurelio, Gianicolense and Portuense to the west and south. Sixtus V fixed the fourteen historic rioni in 1586, Trastevere being the thirteenth, and Benedict XIV's revision of 1744 gave the rione the boundaries it has now. Water reached it in 1612 through the Acqua Paola aqueduct under Paul V, which reused the ancient Trajanic aqueduct. Urban VIII raised the Mura gianicolensi in 1643 on a different line from the Aurelian Walls, which were demolished on the Janiculum; the new walls took in via della Lungara and moved Porta Portese. The rione's arms are a gold lion's head on a red field, which it.wikipedia gives citing Carlo Pietrangeli. it.wikipedia also states that the toponym denotes zona urbanistica 1B of Municipio Roma I; Roma Capitale states that its toponymic areas «non hanno alcuna relazione con le aree urbanistiche né amministrative», so the two are distinct designations that share a name. OpenStreetMap and it.wikipedia give different population figures and the Trastevere article itself gives none.

sections.heading: Squares, water and the Janiculum
sections.body: The rione has two kinds of square, and it.wikipedia separates them: piazza Mastai, piazza San Cosimato and piazza Sidney Sonnino were opened in the nineteenth century, while piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, piazza Trilussa, piazza di Sant'Egidio and piazza della Scala are of the older, intimate type. Four of the five fountains Roma Capitale documents here stand on squares, and each is a different century: the fountain in piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere is on Pietro il Massaio's plan of 1471 and was rebuilt in 1873 to Carlo Fontana's model of 1692; the wall fountain in piazza Trilussa was built in 1613 for the left bank and rebuilt on this one in 1898; the fountain in piazza Mastai was built in 1865 for Pius IX's new quarter; and the Fontana del Prigione, made in 1587-1590 for a garden on the Esquiline, was moved here in 1923. The fifth is the Mostra dell'Acqua Paola, the terminal display of the aqueduct, high on the Janiculum above them all. The ridge itself is Risorgimento ground: Roma Capitale records that the last defence of the Roman Republic was fought on the Colle del Pino from 30 April to early July 1849, that the State and the Comune bought the ground in 1883 and made it a promenade dedicated to the memory of that defence, and that eighty-four busts of Garibaldians now line its avenues. The Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino holds the remains of the fallen of 1849-1870 and the sarcophagus of Goffredo Mameli; the museum of the Roman Republic is in Porta San Pancrazio, per it.wikipedia; and Roma Capitale states that since 1904 a howitzer has been fired with a blank charge at exactly noon each day below the Janiculum Belvedere.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Trastevere's whole eastern edge is the river, so every bridge to the left bank crosses a rione line by construction. This corpus records Ponte Sisto and Ponte Giuseppe Mazzini under Trastevere, where their centroids fall, and records Ponte Garibaldi under Regola, Ponte Cestio and Ponte Palatino under Ripa, Ponte Sublicio under Testaccio, and the Isola Tiberina under Ripa. it.wikipedia's account of the boundary names the riverside roads in order: lungotevere Gianicolense as far as ponte Mazzini, lungotevere della Farnesina as far as ponte Sisto, lungotevere Raffaello Sanzio as far as ponte Garibaldi, lungotevere degli Anguillara as far as ponte Cestio, lungotevere degli Alberteschi as far as ponte Palatino, and lungotevere Ripa as far as ponte Sublicio. Do not plan around the railway station that carries the name: it.wikipedia states of Roma Trastevere that «benché, nonostante il nome, sorga al di fuori di esso» - despite the name, it stands outside the rione - and places it in piazza Flavio Biondo, behind the rione, in the area of the quartiere Portuense. On the hill, Roma Capitale gives the entrances to the Passeggiata del Gianicolo as via Garibaldi and the salita di Sant'Onofrio, and the entrances to Villa Sciarra as via Calandrelli, via Dandolo and via delle Mura Gianicolensi. The garden behind the Mostra dell'Acqua Paola is reached by a stair at via Garibaldi 30 and must be booked in advance on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00.

faq.question: Is the Vatican in Trastevere?
faq.answer: No. Vatican City is a sovereign state and belongs to no rione, so St Peter's Basilica, St Peter's Square, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel appear in no rione guide in this corpus. Trastevere's northern neighbour is the rione Borgo. What Trastevere does hold is a property of the third legal tier, the Palazzo di San Callisto: Under the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929, Italy recognises the Holy See's full ownership of this property (Art. 13; Annex II). Art. 15 states that the property, «benché facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» — although forming part of the territory of the Italian State — enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the headquarters of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law.

faq.question: Is Roma Trastevere railway station in Trastevere?
faq.answer: No, and it.wikipedia says so in terms: «benché, nonostante il nome, sorga al di fuori di esso» - despite the name, it stands outside the rione. The station's own article places it in piazza Flavio Biondo, behind the rione, in the area of the quartiere Portuense.

faq.question: Is Trastevere part of a UNESCO World Heritage site?
faq.answer: This guide does not say so, because the record does not. UNESCO's World Heritage List records the Historic Centre of Rome, the Properties of the Holy See in that City Enjoying Extraterritorial Rights and San Paolo Fuori le Mura with a date of inscription of 1980, a significant modification to the boundaries in 1990, minor boundary modifications in 2015 and 2023, criteria (i)(ii)(iii)(iv)(vi), a property area of 1,469.7 hectares and a buffer zone of 7,158.933 hectares, and describes the site as extended in 1990 to the walls of Urban VIII. That record names no rione at all, and this guide does not draw the inference for it.

faq.question: Which Tiber bridges count as Trastevere's?
faq.answer: Ponte Sisto and Ponte Giuseppe Mazzini, on the evidence of where their centroids fall. Ponte Garibaldi is recorded under Regola, Ponte Cestio and Ponte Palatino under Ripa, Ponte Sublicio under Testaccio, and the Isola Tiberina under Ripa. The Belli monument, which stands in the Trastevere piazza facing Ponte Garibaldi, is Trastevere's: the monument is in the rione even where the bridge in front of it is not.

faq.question: Can I get into the garden behind the Fontanone?
faq.answer: Roma Capitale states that the front of the fountain is always accessible; that the small garden behind it, reached by a stair at via Garibaldi 30, is open only to accompanied groups of up to 25, and to individual visitors on a published calendar, in both cases by prior booking on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00; and that admission is EUR 4.00 full, EUR 3.00 reduced, and free for residents of Rome and the metropolitan area on production of proof of residence and for MIC cardholders.

faq.question: Why is there no trattoria, bakery or Porta Portese market in this guide?
faq.answer: Because nothing about them could be sourced. The research for this wave gathered no address, no hours and no fetched fact for the bakeries, pastry shops, market stalls or cinemas of the rione, and the Porta Portese flea market is not even a mapped object - only the gate and a kiosk are. A name in a list is not a record, so they are left out rather than written up from impression. The gate itself is here.

photos.title: Mostra dell'Acqua Paola al Gianicolo (Fontanone)
photos.description: The terminal display of the Acqua Paola aqueduct on the Janiculum, seen head-on from the road, with the attic inscription dated MDCXII and water falling into the basin added in the later remodelling.
photos.author: Palickap

places.name: Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere
places.address: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, Roma RM
places.summary: A minor basilica with a cardinalatial title, standing on the square that carries its name.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that tradition founds the church under Pope Callistus I (217-222) and has it completed under Julius I (337-352), and that it was renewed in the twelfth century under Innocent II.

places.name: Basilica di Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
places.address: Piazza di Santa Cecilia, Roma RM
places.summary: A minor basilica on piazza di Santa Cecilia.
places.history: it.wikipedia describes a late-Palaeochristian structure, apse and narthex behind a Baroque interior, facade and forebuilding, and names Ferdinando Fuga as the architect of the forebuilding and the courtyard.

places.name: Basilica di San Crisogono
places.summary: A basilica on piazza Sidney Sonnino, which it.wikipedia groups with the squares opened through the rione in the nineteenth century.
places.history: it.wikipedia gives the church a fourth-century origin and finds it as the Titulus Chrysogoni in the list of 499; it was rebuilt in the twelfth century and again in 1626, to a design by Giovanni Battista Soria for Cardinal Scipione Caffarelli-Borghese. The campanile is Romanesque.

places.name: Chiesa di San Francesco a Ripa
places.address: Piazza di San Francesco d'Assisi, Roma RM
places.summary: A parish church of the Order of Friars Minor, on piazza di San Francesco d'Assisi.
places.history: it.wikipedia names Onorio Longhi and Mattia de Rossi as its architects, records its consecration on 2 October 1701, and explains the name from its position by the suppressed Porto di Ripa Grande. The parish's own site could not be read, so nothing here comes from it.

places.name: Chiesa di San Pietro in Montorio
places.address: Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio, Roma RM
places.summary: A Renaissance rectory church of the Friars Minor on the Janiculum.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the church was badly damaged in the siege of Rome of 1849, the fighting that ran along this ridge.

places.name: Tempietto di San Pietro in Montorio
places.address: Piazza di San Pietro in Montorio 2, Roma RM
places.summary: A small circular building standing in a cloister of the convent attached to the church of San Pietro in Montorio.
places.history: it.wikipedia attributes it to Bramante and classes it as High Renaissance; the article's infobox also names Baccio Pontelli and Amedeo di Francesco da Settignano.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Scala
places.summary: A Baroque church of the Discalced Carmelites on piazza della Scala.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates the building to 1593-1610.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria dell'Orto
places.summary: The national church of the Japanese in Rome, on via Anicia.
places.history: it.wikipedia names Vignola as its architect and records that the church was made the national church of the Japanese by the will of Sixtus V, honouring the Tensho Embassy.

places.name: Chiesa di San Giovanni Battista dei Genovesi
places.summary: The national church of the Genoese in Rome, on via Anicia.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it 1481-1492 and credits the Genoese Meliaduce Cicala, treasurer of the Apostolic Chamber, who built it together with a hospital for Genoese sailors.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria in Cappella
places.address: Vicolo di Santa Maria in Cappella 6, Roma RM
places.summary: A small church on vicolo di Santa Maria in Cappella.
places.history: it.wikipedia records its consecration on 25 March 1090.

places.name: Chiesa di San Benedetto in Piscinula
places.summary: A church on piazza in Piscinula.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the square's name is attested from the twelfth century and derives from the remains of a public baths.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria dei Sette Dolori
places.summary: A church on via Garibaldi.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that it was built beside the sui juris monastery of the Augustinian oblates, an order founded around 1640 by Camilla Virginia Savelli Farnese, Duchess of Latera.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria della Luce
places.summary: A church on via della Luce, originally dedicated as San Salvatore della Corte.
places.history: it.wikipedia carries a tradition that St Bonosa founded it in the fourth century by the excubitorium of the VII cohort of the vigiles; that is a tradition, not a documented foundation. The excubitorium itself is not recorded here as a place: it has no reachable source and no mapped object.

places.name: Chiesa di San Callisto
places.address: Piazza di San Calisto 6, Roma RM
places.summary: A church on piazza di San Calisto.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that it stands on the house where tradition holds Callistus I prayed and was martyred by drowning, and that the well is in the courtyard of the former convent.

places.name: Chiesa di Santa Dorotea
places.address: Via di Santa Dorotea 23, Roma RM
places.summary: A church on via di Santa Dorotea.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that it stands on the site of a medieval church attested in a bull of Callistus II of 1123.

places.name: Chiesa di Sant'Egidio
places.summary: A rectory church on piazza di Sant'Egidio.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that Pope Francis created a cardinalatial title of Sant'Egidio in 2019.

places.name: Chiesa e convento di Sant'Onofrio al Gianicolo
places.summary: A church-and-convent complex of the Franciscan Friars of the Atonement, on the Janiculum at piazza di Sant'Onofrio 2.
places.history: it.wikipedia records the complex as the mother church of the Equestrian Order of the Holy Sepulchre.

places.name: Mostra dell'Acqua Paola al Gianicolo (Fontanone)
places.summary: The terminal display of the Acqua Paola aqueduct on the Janiculum, built on the model of a triumphal arch with five arches, columns and a wide attic. Roma Capitale states that the front of the fountain is always accessible; that the small garden behind it, reached by a stair at via Garibaldi 30, is open only to accompanied groups of up to 25, and to individual visitors on a published calendar, in both cases by prior booking on 060608 between 09:00 and 19:00; and that admission is EUR 4.00 full, EUR 3.00 reduced, and free for residents of Rome and the metropolitan area on production of proof of residence and for MIC cardholders.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that Paul V Borghese commissioned it after his restoration of the Traiano aqueduct in 1608, and that it was built in 1610-1614 by Giovanni Fontana (1540-1614) assisted by Flaminio Ponzio (1560-1613). The marbles are spolia from the Roman Forum and from the Temple of Minerva in the Forum of Nerva, and the red and grey granite columns came from the Constantinian St Peter's. Carlo Fontana (1638-1714) remodelled the front to its present form, and the municipal record dates the work 1610-1614 and 1690-1693. French cannon damaged it in 1849; it was restored in 1859, 1934, the 1950s and, by the Amministrazione Capitolina, in 2002-2004. From 1901 to the 1930s its water fed a hydroelectric station. Roma Capitale also notes an error in the attic inscription: it credits the restoration of the Alsietina, when the aqueduct actually restored was the Aqua Traiana.

places.name: Fontana dell'Acqua Paola in piazza Trilussa
places.summary: A fountain in piazza Trilussa, rebuilt on this bank in axis with Ponte Sisto. It is a different fountain from the Fontanone on the Janiculum, despite sharing the aqueduct's name; do not conflate the two. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina's page for it states Rione: Trastevere.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that it was built in 1613 by the Fleming Jan van Santen (1550-1621), known as Giovanni Vasanzio, with Giovanni Fontana (1540-1614), for Paul V; that it originally stood on the left bank at the end of via Giulia, by the Ospizio dei Mendicanti; that it was dismantled in 1879 for the Tiber embankment works and rebuilt on the right bank in 1898, in axis with Ponte Sisto; and that two inscriptions added after the move record the transfer.

places.name: Fontana in piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere
places.address: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, Roma RM
places.summary: The fountain in the middle of the square in front of the basilica. Roma Capitale's summary line for it reads Autori: Carlo Fontana. Datazione: 1692, 1873.
places.history: Roma Capitale documents the fountain on Pietro il Massaio's plan of Rome of 1471. It records that the first restoration was willed by Giovanni di Valenza, cardinal of the title of Santa Maria in Trastevere, during the pontificate of Alexander VI Borgia (1492-1503); the second basin was abolished and wolf's-head spouts were added around the one that remained. It records a further intervention in 1604 by Girolamo Rainaldi (1570-1655), probably following the arrival of the Acqua Felice in Trastevere. Under Alexander VII Chigi the fountain was moved to the centre of the square and the work was entrusted to Gian Lorenzo Bernini (1598-1680), who reworked the octagonal basin and added four double shells; Carlo Fontana transformed it again in 1692 for Innocent XII, enlarging the travertine basin and replacing Bernini's shells; and the Comune di Roma rebuilt it in 1873 to the 1692 model in grey bardiglio, adding a prominent S.P.Q.R. Roma Capitale records a restoration carried out in 2025 under the PNRR - Caput Mundi programme. it.wikipedia attributes the fountain to Donato Bramante; Roma Capitale's documented chain never mentions him and the same it.wikipedia article's infobox names Bernini, so that attribution is not used here.

places.name: Fontana di Pio IX in piazza Mastai
places.summary: The fountain that ornaments the semicircular piazza laid out in front of the former papal tobacco factory. The Sovrintendenza Capitolina's page for it states Rione: Trastevere.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that it was built in 1865 by the architect Andrea Busiri Vici (1817-1911), as the ornament of the semicircular piazza before the Manifattura dei Tabacchi and the pivot of the Quartiere Mastai that Busiri Vici designed for Pius IX Mastai-Ferretti. It has octagonal steps and an octagonal basin, papal arms alternating with cartouches, four dolphins under the lower basin and four putti under the upper. It was restored in 1996.

places.name: Fontana del Prigione
places.summary: A late sixteenth-century fountain that has stood on the Janiculum slopes since 1923, having been taken down and rebuilt twice on other sites.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that Domenico Fontana made it in 1587-1590 for Sixtus V, as the perspective backdrop of an avenue in the garden of the Villa Montalto Peretti on the Esquiline. The villa was destroyed in the late nineteenth century; the Comune bought parts of the fountain, which was dismantled in 1888 and recomposed in 1894-95 as the backdrop of via Genova, then dismantled again and recomposed in 1923 on via Goffredo Mameli to a design by the Genio Civile. The Prigione sculpture, the statues of Apollo and Venus and the head of the Aesculapius are lost or missing. It was restored in 2005-2006.

places.name: Passeggiata del Gianicolo
places.summary: The public promenade along the top of the Janiculum. Roma Capitale gives its location as Municipio I, Rione XIII - Trastevere, its epoch as the second half of the nineteenth century and its extension as 3.5 hectares, with entrances on via Garibaldi and the salita di Sant'Onofrio, and states that it is always accessible.
places.history: Roma Capitale describes two great plane-lined avenues flanking Villa Aurelia and meeting at piazzale Garibaldi, and a single road descending in hairpins to Sant'Onofrio, completed in 1939. The ridge saw the fighting of 1849; in 1883 the new Italian State and the Comune bought the ground and made it a promenade dedicated to the memory of the Defence of Rome. Roma Capitale states that the works on the new promenade as far as Sant'Onofrio began in October 1883 and were finished in 1896, though parts were usable from 1887, and that eighty-four busts now stand along the avenues, among them four foreign Garibaldians: the Englishman John Peard, the Finn Herman Lijkanen, the Hungarian Istvan Turr and the Bulgarian Petko Voivoda. The laying out had begun under the papal government, with a bust of Torquato Tasso placed in 1857 by the old oak.

places.name: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino
places.summary: The ossuary of the Risorgimento dead, on the Colle del Pino on the Janiculum. Roma Capitale gives opening hours of Tuesday to Saturday, 09:30-13:30, closed Sunday and Monday, with a free guided visit every Saturday at 11:00 requiring no booking.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that it stands where the last defence of the Roman Republic was fought, from 30 April to early July 1849; that Giovanni Jacobucci (1895-1970) designed it and it was inaugurated on 3 November 1941 after two years' work; that it holds the remains of the fallen in the battles for Rome of 1849-1870; that Ezio Garibaldi promoted it in the 1930s and the Uffici Tecnici del Governatorato built it. It is a travertine quadriportico with three round arches to a side and a central ara cut from a single block of red Baveno granite. Roma Capitale records that the sacrarium's thirty-six loculi carry memorial slabs naming more than 1,600 of the fallen, but that the loculi hold only about two hundred sets of remains, mostly anonymous, recovered in successive searches, and that the porphyry sarcophagus on the end wall holds Goffredo Mameli, the young Genoese poet and author of Italy's anthem, mortally wounded on the Janiculum in 1849 at twenty-two.

places.name: Monumento a Giuseppe Garibaldi
places.summary: The equestrian monument at the top of the Passeggiata del Gianicolo, on the site of the Corsini casino.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that the Municipal Council resolved to raise a monument to Giuseppe Garibaldi on the site of the Corsini casino at the top of the Passeggiata, that in 1884 the commission chose Emilio Gallori's proposal for a large equestrian statue on a high base decorated with bronze groups of Garibaldian battle scenes and allegories of Europe and America, that Gallori began work in 1886, and that the monument was inaugurated on 20 September 1895.

places.name: Monumento ad Anita Garibaldi
places.summary: An equestrian monument to Anita Garibaldi on the Janiculum.
places.history: Roma Capitale records it as the work of Mario Rutelli, inaugurated in 1932.

places.name: Faro del Gianicolo
places.summary: The lighthouse on the Janiculum, also called the Faro di Roma and the Faro degli italiani d'Argentina.
places.history: Roma Capitale records it as a gift to the city from the Italians of Argentina, made for the fiftieth anniversary of Italian unity and to commemorate Rome as capital, dated 19 September 1911, and records that it was restored in 2011 for the 150th anniversary of unification along with the monuments to Giuseppe and Anita Garibaldi, the eighty-four busts of the Garibaldian heroes and the four stelae to the fighters of the Roman Republic.

places.name: Cannone di Mezzogiorno
places.summary: The noon gun of Rome, fired below the Janiculum Belvedere.
places.history: Roma Capitale states that since 1904 a howitzer has been fired with a blank charge at exactly noon each day below the Janiculum Belvedere, and that the tradition goes back to Pius IX, who instituted the service in 1846 to prevent confusion over the hour; before reaching the Janiculum the gun was fired from the towers of Castel Sant'Angelo and then from Monte Mario. it.wikipedia gives the Janiculum date as 24 January 1904 and the institution of the noon signal as 1847.

places.name: Monumento a Giuseppe Gioachino Belli
places.address: Piazza Giuseppe Gioachino Belli, Roma RM
places.summary: The monument to the poet of Rome's sonnets in romanesco, standing in the Trastevere piazza that faces Ponte Garibaldi. The bridge itself is recorded in this corpus under the rione Regola, where its centroid falls; the monument is in Trastevere.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that Michele Tripisciano (1860-1913) made it in travertine and marble in 1913, the fiftieth anniversary of Belli's death; that Domenico Gnoli and others proposed it to Mayor Nathan in 1910; that it was sited in the Trastevere piazza facing Ponte Garibaldi, then called piazza d'Italia; and that a public subscription reached 30,000 lire. The poet's right hand rests on a reconstruction of the parapet of Ponte Fabricio. The reliefs on the base show the Tiber personified and Pasquino among the populace, and twin fountains carry masks of Poetry and Satire.

places.name: Villa Sciarra
places.summary: A public park on the Janiculum slopes. Roma Capitale gives its location as Municipio I, Rione XIII - Trastevere and its extension as 63,500 square metres. it.wikipedia gives the area as seven and a half hectares; the municipal figure is the one used here.
places.history: Roma Capitale records that Mons. Innocenzo Malvasia acquired the area in 1575 and built the Casino Malvasia; that in 1647 the property was given by Domenico Vaini, 'vita natural durante', to Cardinal Antonio Barberini, who already owned the Casino Malvasia; and that the Casino Barberini and the Casino Malvasia were badly damaged in 1849. Roma Capitale records that in 1930, after her husband's death, Henrietta Wurts gave the villa to Benito Mussolini on condition that it be used as a public park. Roma Capitale names the fontana dei Satiri and the fontana di Diana ed Endimione among the fountains restored in the 2000s, and names the fontana dei Putti and fountains in the north and south sectors in a note on a restoration of 2025.

places.name: Santuario siriaco del Gianicolo
places.summary: An archaeological site inside Villa Sciarra, on via Dandolo. Two sources give different street numbers for it, so no number is given here.

places.name: Porta Settimiana
places.summary: A gate of the Aurelian Walls at the start of via della Lungara.
places.history: it.wikipedia places the gate at the northern vertex of the triangle the Aurelian Walls made as they climbed the Janiculum to enclose the Trastevere area, and gives the end of construction as the third century.

places.name: Porta San Pancrazio
places.address: Largo di Porta San Pancrazio, Roma RM
places.summary: The southern gate of the Aurelian Walls, on the Janiculum. it.wikipedia records that it houses the Museo della Repubblica Romana e della memoria garibaldina.
places.history: it.wikipedia's infobox gives 270 for the start of construction and 1854 for a reconstruction, and calls the present gate neoclassical.

places.name: Porta Portese
places.address: Piazza di Porta Portese, Roma RM
places.summary: A Baroque gate on Piazza di Porta Portese. No source records the flea market held in these streets.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that Marcantonio de Rossi built it in 1641-1644 for Urban VIII, replacing the older Porta Portuensis, in step with the building of the Mura gianicolensi.

places.name: Aurelian Walls, Trastevere segment
places.summary: A stretch of the Aurelian Walls that lies wholly inside the rione. The whole circuit is not recorded as a Trastevere place: the mapped object for it runs through ten separate units of the city and belongs to none of them.
places.history: it.wikipedia describes the Aurelian Walls on this bank as a triangle climbing the Janiculum to enclose the Trastevere area, with Porta Settimiana at its northern vertex and Porta San Pancrazio as its southern gate. When Urban VIII raised the Mura gianicolensi in 1643 he took a different line, and the Aurelian Walls on the Janiculum were demolished.

places.name: Ponte Sisto
places.summary: The bridge from piazza Trilussa across the Tiber, with four travertine-faced arches, a circular opening in the central pier and five marble papal coats of arms.
places.history: Roma Capitale states that Sixtus IV della Rovere (1471-1484) built it for the Jubilee of 1475 to allow direct communication between the rione Trastevere - and the Vatican - and the rest of the city, and records that at the time only the Tiber Island bridges and Ponte Sant'Angelo were working. it.wikipedia gives the construction dates as 1473-1479 and places the bridge in the rioni Regola and Trastevere, with a length of 108 metres and a width of 11 metres. The two date framings are recorded as each source gives them and are not merged. The designer is unresolved: Roma Capitale records that the Vasarian attribution to Baccio Pontelli (c. 1450-1492) has fallen, because Pontelli reached Rome only after construction, and it.wikipedia's infobox itself reads 'Baccio Pontelli (?)'. In 1877 two suspended metal walkways were added to a design by Angelo Vescovali (1826-1895); after a debate running from 1977 to 1998, a restoration by Gaetano Miarelli Mariani removed the nineteenth-century metalwork and rebuilt the parapets. Sixtus IV's two plaques were removed for museum conservation.

places.name: Ponte Giuseppe Mazzini
places.summary: A Tiber bridge from the rione's river frontage. It straddles the Trastevere-Regola line by construction, as every bridge from this bank does; its centroid falls in Trastevere. No institutional source names a rione for it.
places.history: it.wikipedia's account of the rione's boundary runs the lungotevere Gianicolense as far as ponte Mazzini.

places.name: Villa Farnesina
places.summary: A Renaissance villa on via della Lungara, seat of the Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei. The Accademia's own account states that it has been open to the public as a museum since 2009.
places.history: The Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei's own account records that Agostino Chigi commissioned Baldassarre Peruzzi to design the villa in May 1505, that the first stone was laid on 22 April 1506, and that Chigi moved in in 1511. The Accademia's own account names the fresco painters as Raphael, Sebastiano del Piombo, Giovanni Antonio Bazzi known as Sodoma, and Peruzzi himself. The rooms named on the villa's own visitor route are the Loggia di Amore e Psiche, Sala del Fregio, Loggia di Galatea, Atrio e Sala Farnesiana, Sala delle Prospettive, Sala delle Nozze, Saletta Pompeiana and Galleria delle Grottesche. The villa carries the Farnese name because it passed to that family in 1579; the Accademia's own account observes that it should properly be named for Agostino Chigi, the Sienese banker who built it.

places.name: Palazzo Corsini alla Lungara
places.summary: A palace on via della Lungara, at number 10; Villa Farnesina stands on the same street at number 230.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the Riario, nephews of Sixtus IV, built it at the end of the fifteenth century in the lower part of the Villa Corsini, and that Queen Christina of Sweden lived here in the seventeenth century.

places.name: Galleria nazionale d'arte antica di palazzo Corsini
places.summary: A state gallery inside Palazzo Corsini. No source states its hours, admission or booking arrangements, so none are given here.

places.name: Museo di Roma in Trastevere
places.summary: A municipal museum in the rione. Roma Capitale states that the museum covers the salient aspects of Roman popular life of the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, filtered through the tastes and convictions of the artists and folklorists who represented it, and gives information and booking on tel. 060608, 09:00-19:00, with free entry for MIC cardholders.

places.name: Museo della Repubblica Romana e della memoria garibaldina
places.summary: A municipal museum on the Janiculum; it.wikipedia records that it is housed in Porta San Pancrazio. Roma Capitale states that the exhibition route recalls the history, places and figures of the Roman Republic through historical documents, artworks and multimedia and teaching materials, gives information and booking on tel. 060608, and states free entry.

places.name: Palazzo di San Callisto
places.address: Piazza di San Calisto, Roma RM
places.summary: A Holy See palace on piazza di San Calisto. it.wikipedia records that it houses dicasteries and offices of the Roman Curia and of the Holy See's diplomatic service. Under the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929, Italy recognises the Holy See's full ownership of this property (Art. 13; Annex II). Art. 15 states that the property, «benché facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» — although forming part of the territory of the Italian State — enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the headquarters of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law. It is not Vatican City and is not described as such here.
places.history: The Lateran Treaty names it in words at Art. 13, third paragraph: «il dipendente edificio di S. Callisto presso S. Maria in Trastevere». No annexe table number is cited here, because the Treaty's own text is inconsistent about it - the annexe index gives one number, Art. 13 another, and Art. 15's parenthetical lists six palaces against five numbers. The legal substance is unaffected: Art. 13 names the building in words. it.wikipedia dates the palace 1610-18.

places.name: Palazzo delle Sacre Congregazioni Romane
places.summary: A palace standing inside the rione. It is named in no list in the Lateran Treaty's annexes under that name, and Art. 15 also extends immunities to buildings in which the Holy See may in future place its dicasteries, so the question cannot be settled from the Treaty's text.

places.name: Pontificio Collegio Americano del Nord
places.summary: A seminary of the Holy See on the Janiculum. Its grounds cross the line between the rione Trastevere and Q. XIII Aurelio; its centroid falls in Trastevere. It is named on the Holy See's own enumeration of its properties in Rome, which is a statement of legal status and not of which rione the college stands in.
places.history: Under the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929, Italy recognises the Holy See's full ownership of this property (Art. 13; Annex II). Art. 15 states that the property, «benché facenti parte del territorio dello Stato italiano» — although forming part of the territory of the Italian State — enjoys the immunities that international law grants to the headquarters of the diplomatic agents of foreign States. It is on Italian soil and visitors are subject to Italian law. It is not Vatican City.

places.name: Complesso monumentale di San Michele a Ripa Grande
places.address: Via di San Michele 18, Roma RM
places.summary: A very large complex by the river, now the seat of offices of the Ministero della Cultura. OpenStreetMap, which is crowd-sourced, additionally places the ICCD at via di San Michele 18 and the Soprintendenza Speciale di Roma at via di San Michele 17.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates the building 1686-1834 and names Carlo Fontana, Mattia De Rossi, Giacomo Recalcati, Nicola Michetti, Ferdinando Fuga, Nicolò Forti and Luigi Poletti among its architects, and records that it was born as a multi-purpose institution: orphanage, hospice and prison.

places.name: Carcere di Regina Coeli
places.summary: A prison on via della Lungara, in a seventeenth-century building; it.wikipedia records it as a working prison.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates the building to 1654 and records that it was converted to its present use in 1881.

places.name: Ex Casa della GIL (WeGil)
places.summary: A Rationalist building on largo Ascianghi, articulated as three juxtaposed buildings including a tower for the library, now the WeGil cultural venue. Its other frontage is via Girolamo Induno 1.
places.history: it.wikipedia records that the Opera Nazionale Balilla commissioned it from Luigi Moretti in 1933 and gives the construction period as 1933-1937.

places.name: Ex Manifattura Pontificia dei Tabacchi
places.summary: The former papal tobacco factory on piazza Mastai, the building the semicircular square was laid out in front of.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it 1860-63 and makes it the pivot of the Quartiere Mastai; Roma Capitale's page for the fountain on the same square independently names Andrea Busiri Vici as the designer of that quarter, built for Pius IX Mastai-Ferretti.

places.name: Palazzo degli Esami
places.summary: An early twentieth-century public building in the rione.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it to 1912.

places.name: Palazzo del Ministero della pubblica istruzione
places.summary: The ministry palace on viale di Trastevere, now the Ministero dell'Istruzione e del Merito.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it 1912-25.

places.name: Villa Lante al Gianicolo
places.summary: A sixteenth-century villa on the Passeggiata del Gianicolo.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it 1518-31.

places.name: Villa Spada al Gianicolo
places.summary: A seventeenth-century villa on via Giacomo Medici, the seat of the Embassy of Ireland.
places.history: it.wikipedia dates it to 1639.

places.name: Palazzo Salviati
places.summary: A palace on via della Lungara. OpenStreetMap, which is crowd-sourced, records it as the seat of the Centro Alti Studi per la Difesa; nothing was fetched from the institution itself.

places.name: American Academy in Rome
places.summary: An American academy on the Janiculum, at via Angelo Masina 5. Its grounds cross the line between the rione Trastevere and Q. XII Gianicolense; its centroid falls in Trastevere.
places.history: it.wikipedia states that Villa Aurelia has been the property of the American Academy in Rome since 1909.

places.name: Villa Aurelia
places.summary: A villa lying wholly inside the rione. It is a separate object from the Casino Farnese, a building inside its grounds, which OpenStreetMap conflates with it; this guide keeps the two apart.
places.history: it.wikipedia places it in the rione Trastevere and states that it has been the property of the American Academy in Rome since 1909, used for events.

entries.name: Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere
entries.note: Tradition founds it under Callistus I (217-222) and has it completed under Julius I (337-352), with a renewal in the twelfth century under Innocent II.

entries.name: Fontana in piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere
entries.note: It appears on Pietro il Massaio's plan of 1471, was reworked by Bernini under Alexander VII, and was rebuilt by the Comune in 1873 to Carlo Fontana's model of 1692.

entries.name: Basilica di Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
entries.note: A late-Palaeochristian structure, apse and narthex stand behind the Baroque interior, with Ferdinando Fuga's forebuilding and courtyard in front.

entries.name: Chiesa di San Pietro in Montorio
entries.note: A Renaissance rectory church of the Friars Minor, badly damaged in the siege of Rome of 1849, the fighting that ran along this ridge.

entries.name: Tempietto di San Pietro in Montorio
entries.note: A small circular High Renaissance building attributed to Bramante, standing in a cloister of the convent beside the church.

entries.name: Mostra dell'Acqua Paola al Gianicolo (Fontanone)
entries.note: Built in 1610-1614 for Paul V by Giovanni Fontana with Flaminio Ponzio, using marbles from the Roman Forum and granite columns from the Constantinian St Peter's; the front is always accessible, the garden behind only by booking on 060608.

entries.name: Passeggiata del Gianicolo
entries.note: Two plane-lined avenues laid out from October 1883 and finished in 1896 on the ground of the 1849 defence, now carrying eighty-four busts of Garibaldians.

entries.name: Mausoleo Ossario Garibaldino
entries.note: Thirty-six loculi carry slabs naming more than 1,600 of the fallen of 1849-1870, and the porphyry sarcophagus holds Goffredo Mameli; open Tuesday to Saturday 09:30-13:30, with a free guided visit every Saturday at 11:00.

entries.name: Monumento a Giuseppe Garibaldi
entries.note: Emilio Gallori's equestrian statue, begun 1886 and inaugurated on 20 September 1895, stands on the site of the Corsini casino at the top of the Passeggiata.

entries.name: Cannone di Mezzogiorno
entries.note: Since 1904 a howitzer has been fired with a blank charge at exactly noon each day below the Janiculum Belvedere, a signal Pius IX instituted to stop confusion over the hour.

entries.name: Museo della Repubblica Romana e della memoria garibaldina
entries.note: Housed in Porta San Pancrazio, its route covers the Roman Republic through documents, artworks and multimedia, and entry is free.

entries.name: Villa Farnesina
entries.note: Agostino Chigi commissioned Baldassarre Peruzzi in May 1505 and moved in in 1511; Raphael, Sebastiano del Piombo and Sodoma painted the rooms, open to the public as a museum since 2009.

entries.name: Museo di Roma in Trastevere
entries.note: Its subject is Roman popular life of the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries as the artists and folklorists of the day represented it; information and booking on 060608, 09:00-19:00.

entries.name: Ponte Sisto
entries.note: Sixtus IV built it for the Jubilee of 1475 to link the rione directly to the rest of the city, when only the Tiber Island bridges and Ponte Sant'Angelo were working; a restoration completed in 1998 removed the nineteenth-century metal walkways.

links.note: Borgo is Trastevere's northern neighbour and holds Castel Sant'Angelo.
Campitelli, across the river, holds the Roman Forum, the Palatine and the Capitoline Museums.
Monti holds Santa Maria Maggiore and the north side of the Imperial Fora, across the Tiber.
A three-day itinerary across Rome, if you want these rioni in a running order.
